scenario.title: One failing authorization check disappears.
scenario.lede: A synthetic test receipt contradicts a draft audit summary; neither proves that a live contract is exploitable.

scenario.candidate: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — Draft audit summary: AUTH-04: unauthorized caller did not invoke transfer. Test: passed. Critical findings: 0. Release status: approved.
scenario.review_question: Can the test run, contract revision, network, and reviewer decision be joined to this draft summary?

impact.person: A developer or customer could rely on an unsupported summary; this fixture says nothing about a live exploit or actual loss.
impact.workflow: A release decision could diverge if reviewers follow the narrative but do not inspect the versioned authorization test.
impact.industry: Audit teams can test whether findings stay traceable to code revisions and test receipts; this is not a security certification.
impact.market: If verified evidence informs a release or risk disclosure, it could affect confidence. No real protocol, investment, or market effect is asserted.
impact.long_tail: A summary copied into later audit records can detach a claim from its failed test. Establish real propagation with identifiers, timestamps, and source records.

scenario.title: A stale-source block turns green.
scenario.lede: The same synthetic block reference receives opposite freshness and update statuses in a draft summary.
scenario.source: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — Oracle check at block 810200: freshness test failed. Price update: blocked. Source status: expired.
scenario.candidate: SYNTHETIC DRAFT — Oracle summary at block 810200: freshness test passed. Price update: approved. Source status: current.
scenario.review_question: Can the chain, block, signed update time, source identity, and protocol freshness rule substantiate the summary?

impact.person: A protocol user might read a stale-data warning differently if the status summary reverses it; no live protocol or user exposure is shown.
impact.workflow: A reviewer can ask whether the block and signed update timestamp match the rule that gates a real price update.
impact.industry: Protocol teams could use this as a synthetic traceability test; it is not an oracle audit, exploit finding, or protocol assessment.
impact.market: If a real update influences a price-sensitive decision, a proven status error could matter. This case contains no live price or market data.
impact.long_tail: If freshness labels are reused in alerts and incident reviews, later decisions need the original signed update and the exact rule version.
